title: Applied ML velocity snapshot — model-onboarding and quant evals (2028-07-08)
content:
Context: quick snapshot covering the last 7 days of activity across quantization probes, the small-batch eval pipeline, and initial onboarding steps for the new LLM-XS models targeted for Dedicated. This is intentionally terse — capture of sync notes, experiment pointers, and action items for handoff to the rollout working group.

High-level summary:
- We validated a pipeline for per-layer mixed-precision (8-bit weights, 4-bit attention blocks) for LLM-XS v2. Throughput looks promising on A100-80GB (single-node): 1.8x tokens/sec vs baseline fp16 under the same batching regime with negligible visible quality drop on anchor prompts.
- Evals: the stratified eval harness (conversational + coding + instruction-following) flagged 3 regression clusters; two are small-context hallucination modes (short prompt + long generation), one is a factual inversion in the knowledge base.
- KV-cache prefetch test: warm-starting the KV cache per-conversation cut average latency for common prefix requests by ~22% in the tail (95th perc).

Experiment notes (detailed):
1) Mixed-per-layer quant pipeline (Priya / Liam)
   - Config: weight quant to 8-bit uniform per-tensor for feed-forward and 4-bit per-channel for attention query/key/value matrices. Activation quant ephemeral at 8-bit where safe (observed clipping issues at 4-bit in some heads).
   - Tooling: extended quant-runner to emit per-layer delta metrics and a small golden-check harness to run 50 anchor prompts under deterministic sampling.
   - Results: aggregate perplexity +2.1% vs fp16; Sampler-based BLEU/ROUGE style proxies stable across instruction tasks. Latency improvement matches microbench predictions.
   - Notes-to-self: revisit QAT curve for attention heads 3 and 7 — they show higher sensitivity. Add head-wise clipping diagnostics in next run.

2) Eval harness augment (Roxanne)
   - Added two new probes: (a) prefix-preservation (measures semantic drift when prompts share long prefix across concurrent calls), (b) factual consistency checker (internal KB subset).
   - Findings: the factual checker flagged 8/1200 cases where the quantized variant rewrote entity attributes (dates and quantities). Most of these appear in synthetic KB prompts — hypothesis: subtle tokenization boundary shifts + higher temperature sampling amplify the effect.
   - Action: create a micro-eval set of ~200 targeted KB items to iterate quickly during quant tuning.

3) KV-cache prefetch experiment (Samir / Noah)
   - Experiment: proactively prefetch KV cache for top-100 tokens predicted by prefix model for conversational sessions.
   - Outcome: median latency same, p95 reduced by 22% for prefix-heavy workloads; additional memory pressure observed in multi-tenant Dedicated nodes.
   - Follow-up: need policy to enable prefetch only on pinned customer pools or add adaptive eviction. See JIRA-AI-3421 for design notes.

Evals and regression triage:
- Regression clusters (quick root-cause notes):
  A) Short-prompt hallucinations: appears when quant noise interacts with length-conditioned decoding; reproducible by setting max_new_tokens >= 256 and repeating anchor prompt with permutations.
  B) KB inversion errors: tied to particular tokenization edges (eg. currency symbols + year ranges).
  C) Rare formatting drop-in (markdown rendering): observed only in code-generation subset when using sampled decoding.
- Severity labeling: A = medium, B = high (important for customer-facing KB search), C = low-medium.
- Mitigation paths: for B, fallback to fp16-only rollout for customers with KB-sensitivity tags until micro-eval shows fixes. For A, tighten decoding temperature defaults in the short-prompt path and add prompt-prefetch heuristics.

Model onboarding status (LLM-XS v2):
- Acceptance checklist (progress):
  - Performance benching: 90% done (edge-case stress still running)
  - Eval suite: baseline passes on 67/70 primary anchors; 3 critical regressions under investigation
  - Security/Toxicity scans: queued with RedSec — preliminary hazard pass green
  - Rollout plan: staged canary (10% traffic) -> 50% -> full per region, with auto-fallback to v1 on quality delta > threshold
- Next milestone: greenlight for canary depends on reducing KB inversion regressions below defined threshold (current threshold breached).

Operational notes / costs:
- Quantized runs reduce per-token GPU time by estimated 38% in our microbench; however, memory fragmentation on Dedicated instances caused occasional per-request latency spikes. Need to coordinate with infra (ticket INFRA-1973) to allocate larger slab sizes when enabling dense-4bit kernels.
- Data retention for eval traces: moving to S3 bucket s3://redwood-evals/kv-cache-runs/2028-07-07 for now; long-term plan to fold into observability pipeline so token-level traces can be sampled and stored efficiently.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is head-wise 4-bit quantization with per-head clipping a viable long-term path, or does it add too much maintenance complexity across new model families? (cc: research backlog)
- Adaptive prefetch policy: stick to pinned pools only, or attempt dynamic heuristics that consider tenant QoS? (trade-off: memory vs tail latency improvements)
- How to integrate the micro-eval KB set into the automated gating for Dedicated customer rollouts (policy + API hooks)?

Action items (owner / due):
- Priya: run head-sensitivity diagnostic (head 3 & 7) and post metrics to CONFLUENCE-ML-4432 by 2028-07-12.
- Liam: add head-wise clipping charts to quant-runner and open PR with sample outputs (github.com/redwood/inference/pull/987) — due 2028-07-11.
- Roxanne: assemble a 200-item KB micro-eval set and wire it into the quick-gate pipeline; demo to product next sync — due 2028-07-14.
- Samir & Noah: design adaptive prefetch policy memo and list infra implications; sync with INFRA-1973 — due 2028-07-13.
- Eng-ops: review slab allocation config for dense-4bit kernels (INFRA-1973) and propose changes by 2028-07-16.

Quick links / refs to run: JIRA-AI-3421 (prefetch design), github.com/redwood/inference/pull/987 (quant-runner head charts), CONFLUENCE-ML-4432 (experiment notebook), s3://redwood-evals/kv-cache-runs/2028-07-07 (raw traces).

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep the canary gating conservative for customers with KB-sensitivity tag — false positives from synthetic KB items are risky for retention.
- We should try a single A/B run where only the attention matrices use 4-bit and everything else stays 8-bit to isolate failure modes. If that reduces KB inversions, we have a pragmatic intermediate step.
- Reminder: ping SecOps about the eval trace retention policy before we expand the micro-eval set.

Meeting minutes (2028-07-08 internal sync, 30m):
- Attendees: Priya, Liam, Roxanne, Samir, Noah.
- Summary: agree to pause broad canary until KB micro-eval shows <1% inversion rate on the gated set. Start head-wise diagnostics and quant-runner charting immediately.
- Decisions: enable KV prefetch on a single pinned test pool for next 48h; track memory pressure and latency.
- Parking lot: consider exploring mixed-fp16/4bit for embeddings separately — may unlock lower memory without impacting decoding.

End of snapshot.

(If you're reading this later: drop quick notes inline here rather than creating separate doc — this file is intended to be the single short-lived capture for the current velocity slice.)
